witness.note: n = 5 lies in the stated domain [1,50]. Exact integer arithmetic, no floating point. The proposition fails at n = 5 and at 45 further points; it holds only for n in {1,2,3,4}, where floor(n/5) = 0.

search_bound: Exhaustive over the entire stated domain: all 50 integers n with 1 <= n <= 50. This is not a bounded search in the incomplete sense - the domain is finite and was enumerated in full with exact Python integers.
broken_step: s2. The claim is FALSE, so no argument could establish it, but the specific false step is s2: it asserts F(n+1) - F(n) = (n+1)^3 for every 1 <= n <= 49 where F(n) = (n(n+1)/2)^2 + floor(n/5). This fails whenever floor((n+1)/5) > floor(n/5), i.e. at n = 4, 9, 14, 19, 24, 29, 34, 39, 44, 49 (10 counterexamples); e.g. F(5) - F(4) = 126, not 125. Steps s3-s8 are individually true but inert - they are not used by the conclusion. s9 then invokes 'base case and increment' on the broken s2.
